manager_rule: Detect and serialize Rule-33 + Rule-50 co-firing. After evaluating round R: if Rule 33 fires for cable index C_sym (both /SENSEC{C_sym}_HI and /SENSEC{C_sym}_LO appear in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines') AND Rule 50 also fires for a DIFFERENT cable index C_asym (exactly one member of the /SENSEC{C_asym}_HI or /SENSEC{C_asym}_LO pair appears in failing_reasons with 'has unconnected ratlines' while the other member does NOT appear in failing_reasons) in the SAME round R: (1) in round R+1, inject ONLY Rule 33's Kelvin force stubs for cable C_sym (/SENSEC{C_sym}_HI and /SENSEC{C_sym}_LO) using mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics per Rule 34 — suppress the Rule-50 single-member stub for cable C_asym for round R+1 only; (2) in round R+2, inject the Rule-50 single-member stub for cable C_asym (the unrouted member identified in round R) using mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics per Rule 34, regardless of whether cable C_sym's Kelvin gate cleared in round R+1; (3) all other active rules (Rule 46 absorber bypass, Rule 48 keepout injection, Rule 33 force stubs) proceed for rounds R+1 and R+2 per their own trigger conditions — only the Rule-50 stub is deferred, not suppressed permanently; (4) log 'rule33_rule50_cofire_serialization' with fields: (a) round number R at trigger, (b) symmetric cable index C_sym, (c) asymmetric cable index C_asym, (d) which member of C_asym is deferred (e.g. /SENSEC2_HI), (e) the round R+2 in which the deferred stub will be injected, (f) kelvin_unrouted, DRC, and unconnected from round R. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 40-50 and does not modify net_absorption_count, compiler_excluded_nets, or any other session-scoped state maintained by those rules. It does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate for conditions other than the Rule-50 stub timing. Rationale: round 94 is the first observed round where cable-1 symmetric failure (Rule 33) and cable-2 asymmetric failure (Rule 50) co-occur, with no existing rule governing their relative priority. Both generate absorber-bypassing force stubs targeting the same congested shunt-cluster exit region in the same round (R+1), creating maximal inter-cable routing contention. Serializing across rounds gives cable C_sym exclusive routing priority in the shared exit corridor during R+1 before cable C_asym re-enters in R+2, reducing the per-round competing-stub pressure at the narrowest point of the Kelvin escape path.
